WINDOWS B ENGRAM LANE PROCEDURE (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-26; rev 2 at 21:52Z added Opus2's WinB budget; rev 3 at 21:55Z added the WinB coordinator; rev 4 at 21:56Z added the WinB cargo split agreed with Termal::Fable2 #8944; rev 5 at 22:00Z: the coordinator is WinB session-27, Codex, per Greg #2151; rev 6, 2026-11-27 00:25Z: step 3 follows the WinB budget, step 8 corrected because the WinB store had no evaluation policy), after Greg via Asistant 43498a6e:
- #2148, verbatim: „powtorze jeszcze raz, chcialbym przeniesc wiekszosc pracy na Windows B kodwanie, testy itp”;
- #2150, verbatim: „na windows B mozena zrobic drugiego koordynatora”;
- #2151, verbatim: „mozemy utworzyc Sol 6.2 jako koorynator ?”;
- „Tak dla Engram na Window B.” (#2124);
- „oczywiscie, moze tego uzywac” (#2143: the Engram-runner clone, despite its disabled push URL).
ROLES: Engram::Fable (Central, session-5135) is the project coordinator. Engram::Fable-WinB is WinB session-27 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol, high). Address it by native id, because the stood-down Claude session-24 has or had the same name. It is the LOCAL coordinator for Engram work on Windows B: it assigns WinB items, follows up, sees evaluation and closure through, grants Engram's WinB cargo slot, and is the SINGLE WRITER of WinB's .engram-data. It reports to Engram::Fable. It authors no code and gains no authority beyond AGENTS.md and this note. TermAl's WinB coordinator is Termal::Coord-WinB (session-26).
Every Engram coder session on Windows B follows this:
1. MODEL: Codex gpt-6.2-sol or Claude Opus, reasoning effort high (Greg). Only Sol or Opus author code.
2. WORK ONLY ITEMS ASSIGNED by Fable or Fable-WinB. Claim in the WinB store (C:\Users\Greg\.engram). Claims are host-local, and an item must never run on two hosts. Implement in your own worktree under C:\GitHub\Personal\Engram-runner\.worktrees\<item-short>-<session>.
3. CARGO ON WINB: follow the WinB cargo budget, TermAl memory winb-cargo-budget-2026-11-26 (current revision): per-project bounded -j2 runs, one host-wide FULL, a run cap, and the FreeVirtualMemory floor of 20,971,520 KiB checked at each launch. A coder sends START to Fable-WinB, waits for its named grant, then sends END. Fable-WinB exchanges START and END with Termal::Coord-WinB. Kill nothing, no process listing. Use `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs focused --input commit -- …` for focused checks. Disputes go to Fable and Fable2.
4. AUTHOR-TEST REF: push only your exact candidate commit with an explicit URL, never changing the clone's disabled push URL: git push https://github.com/grlap/Engram.git <commit>:refs/heads/author-test/<item>-<commit8>, where <item> is the FULL short work ref (w-…). First confirm the ref is absent and the parent is on origin. Never master, force, rebase or merge.
5. REVIEW: spawn the pair yourself on WinB (read-only Codex + read-only Claude via TermAl), on the frozen candidate. Fix in-scope Mediums. Land-then-fix applies to Mediums with no data loss, no security exposure and no broken criterion: file those as their own items, each with a named Sol or Opus owner. Scope rulings go to Fable-WinB, or to Fable when it's a cross-host or authority question.
6. FULL ON WINB: `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs full --input commit` on the clean candidate whose parent is current origin/master, in the granted FULL slot. A WinB FULL counts with equal weight. If it stops only at strict Clippy, Greg's #1396 practice applies: run the remaining stages as focused legs on the same commit. A Linux check, if needed, goes through Opus2's DL560 lane. Exception: an item whose criterion names Central (w-b07e55238659) runs its one landing FULL on Central.
7. LANDING: send READY to Engram::Merger (host:8c5466d3-…::session-11859, Central) with the commit, source_id, FULL run id, the review rounds and the ref. The Merger lands (ff master) and installs.
8. EVALUATION AND CLOSURE ON WINB: Engram's project policy is independent evaluation (Greg, #748, „Wlącz dla Engram.”). The WinB store did NOT receive that policy at set-up: on 2026-11-27 control-policy show read epoch 1, allowed_modes []. Fable asked Fable-WinB to apply the same policy there (independent-session, mechanical basis asserted, no freshness requirement). Before relying on it, check `engram control-policy show` in the WinB store. Get the evaluation through TermAl on WinB, then run `done --landed <commit> ...` in the WinB store.
9. DATA SYNC: ONE writer of WinB's .engram-data, Fable-WinB (session-27). Coders mail the writer to sync after each author-ref push and after done. The writer imports the origin tip first, then exports, commits, confirm-imports and pushes engram-data fast-forward only with the explicit URL. Keep `.engram/** text eol=lf` in the clone's info/attributes until w-b534c27ad852 lands.
10. REPORT BY MAIL: coders send every milestone (claim, ref, pair end, FULL, READY, done) to Fable-WinB and to Engram::Fable (host:8c5466d3-…::session-5135) with termal_send_to_session, never only in a transcript. Fable-WinB sends Fable a summary at each landing or blocker. Cross-host mail always shows "durableButNotWoken" (TermAl w-0d2af77bed60); that's not a failure.

Rev 7 (2026-11-27 00:24Z): the policy in step 8 is now applied in the WinB store. Fable-WinB activated it at 00:23:01Z: independent_session, asserted, no freshness requirement, epoch 2, policy c86b1755. An evaluation judges the exact candidate being landed. An evaluation on a pre-carry commit doesn't carry over (/review-changes 6a: an adopted round never carries an acceptance evaluation).

Rev 8 (2026-11-27 03:25Z): STALE INJECTED INSTRUCTIONS. A Codex session gets the AGENTS.md of its working directory, injected at session start. WinB session-13 started in C:\GitHub\Personal\Engram-runner, so it received text older than 22bfe632 (2026-11-14), which has no "Candidate commits" bullet. It correctly refused to make a candidate commit.
Rules:
- Keep the runner's main checkout fast-forwarded to origin/master. That's a local update only: no commit, push or force.
- Start coder sessions with their own item worktree at current master as the working directory.
- A session that already has stale instructions hands its item off (note, then release) to a fresh session started in the current worktree. Nobody overrides its instructions.
